records.name: Delta Phi Epsilon Sorority Inc
records.notes: National social sorority, headquartered at 251 S Camac Street, Philadelphia. Hidden as private. Membership is by campus recruitment: the How To Join page sends people to their campus Fraternity and Sorority Life office, refers to an invitation to membership, and has separate legacy and alumnae routes. The Volunteer page has an Apply Now link, but it describes national volunteer committees, not a Philadelphia program, so it does not make this a local public group. Status is active on year-only evidence: the homepage shows an International Governing Board 2026 item and scholarship awards for academic year 2026, with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. Owner decision point: if social sororities should be listed as student groups, this could flip to publish with open_to students and newcomer friendliness 2, because recruitment comes before you see what it is like. The 12 other batch entries under this exact name and address are marked duplicate of this record. Personal contact names from the IRS filings were not recorded.

records.notes: Collegiate chapter of the national sorority in the primary record. The national site does not name this chapter's campus, and the Chapter Locator, which lists chapters, was not opened, so its location and any public activity are unknown. Hidden as private for the same reason as the national record: membership is by campus recruitment, not an open sign up.

records.name: Delta Sigma Iota Fraternity
records.notes: Collegiate fraternity with a South Asian culture focus; chapters listed include Penn State. Hidden as private: the site offers no membership path beyond general inquiries and campus expansion, and no program a visitor could attend or volunteer with. Its inquiry emails are hidden by email protection, so none are recorded. The page mentions a new expansion colony at Temple University, but a follow up search found no corroborating source, so that claim is unconfirmed. Status is unknown: the only dates are a 2024 statistic and a copyright footer, and neither counts as evidence of activity. The IRS filing gives an apartment address, which is not recorded because it may be a person's home. Owner decision point: if Temple recruitment counts as a public way in, this could flip to publish with open_to students once a Temple source is confirmed.

notes: Batch had 15 entries. Thirteen are the same national sorority, Delta Phi Epsilon Sorority Inc, under 13 EINs with the same name, mailing address and website. The first (delta-phi-epsilon-sorority-inc-19107-29) is the primary record and the other 12 are verdict duplicate. The Phi Pi chapter and Delta Sigma Iota are separate records. Verdict counts: hide 3 (all private), duplicate 12, publish 0. No record met the public join bar from the group's own pages, so nothing is published. Two decisions for the owner are flagged in the records: whether social sororities and collegiate fraternities should be listed as student groups. Delta Sigma Iota's Temple colony claim is unconfirmed by search. Delta Sigma Iota's inquiry emails are protected from reading, so none are recorded. No pages were blocked, and no bot checks were hit. Searches: 1 of 2 used. Fetches: 5 used. Budget was not exhausted; the batch was handled with one check per organization plus the sorority's How To Join and Volunteer pages.
